title: One Pipeline object so preprocessing cannot escape the fold
prescribes: Put every fitted transformation inside a Pipeline / ColumnTransformer so cross-validation refits it per fold; never transform the full dataset before splitting.
applied: Built a ColumnTransformer over 11 numeric and 16 categorical churn columns, cross-validated it correctly, and measured what the pre-fitted alternative reports instead.
narrative: The pipeline expands 27 input columns into 50 model features (median imputation and scaling on the numeric block, most-frequent imputation and one-hot with a min-frequency floor on the categorical block), and all of it is refitted inside every CV fold.
Cross-validated correctly it scores 0.8458 +/- 0.0027 ROC-AUC. Fitting the same preprocessing on train and test first and then cross-validating reports 0.8459 -- a difference of +0.0001.

That gap is small precisely because this preprocessing is mild; scaling barely leaks. The reason to be strict anyway is that the same mistake with target encoding, imputation from group means, or feature selection produces a large gap, and the code looks identical. The Pipeline makes the correct version the easy version.
On the untouched test split the fitted pipeline scores 0.8490, consistent with the cross-validated estimate -- which is what a non-leaking setup should look like.

charts.title: Per-fold ROC-AUC: correct pipeline vs pre-fitted preprocessing

code_excerpt:
pre = ColumnTransformer([
    ('num', Pipeline([('impute', SimpleImputer(strategy='median')),
                      ('scale', StandardScaler())]), NUM),
    ('cat', Pipeline([('impute', SimpleImputer(strategy='most_frequent')),
                      ('onehot', OneHotEncoder(handle_unknown='ignore', min_frequency=20))]), CAT),
])
pipe = Pipeline([('prep', pre), ('clf', LogisticRegression(class_weight='balanced'))])
cross_val_score(pipe, X_train, y_train, cv=StratifiedKFold(5, shuffle=True), scoring='roc_auc')
takeaway: Wrapping preprocessing in the estimator costs nothing and removes an entire class of silent optimism; with scaling and one-hot alone the optimism is only +0.0001 AUC, but the identical mistake with target encoding or group-mean imputation is worth far more.
